title: Seattle by the Sound
summary: Seven days of Pike Place, ferries and salmon, glass art and rock history, and green parks with views of the Sound and the mountains.
author: friends of Placemoir

places.name: Fairmont Olympic Hotel
places.notes: Seattle's grand 1924 hotel. Classic rooms and an easy walk to the market and the art museum.

places.name: Inn at the Market
places.notes: A small hotel right at the market. Book a room facing Elliott Bay.

places.name: The Edgewater
places.notes: Built on a pier over Elliott Bay, where the Beatles once fished from their window.

places.name: Ace Hotel Seattle
places.notes: Simple, stylish rooms in Belltown, some with a shared bath. The budget pick.

places.name: Pike Place Chowder
places.notes: Award-winning chowders in a tiny spot off Post Alley. Get the New England in a bread bowl.

places.name: Piroshky Piroshky
places.notes: Russian hand pies baked all day. The smoked salmon pâté one is the classic.

places.name: Beecher's Handmade Cheese
places.notes: Watch cheese being made through the window, then get the mac and cheese.

places.name: Matt's in the Market
places.notes: Seasonal Northwest dinners upstairs in the market, looking out at the famous clock.

places.name: The Pink Door
places.notes: Italian-American food behind an unmarked pink door, with a deck over the bay.

places.name: Elliott's Oyster House
places.notes: Dozens of Northwest oysters on Pier 56. Come for the afternoon oyster happy hour.

places.name: Taylor Shellfish Oyster Bar
places.notes: A shellfish farm's own oyster bar. Geoduck if you're brave, Kumamotos if you're not.

places.name: Salumi
places.notes: Cured meat sandwiches in Pioneer Square. The porchetta is worth the lunch line.

places.name: Canlis
places.notes: The special night out since 1950, with a glass dining room above Lake Union. Book well ahead.

places.name: Paseo
places.notes: Caribbean roast pork sandwiches dripping with caramelized onions. Grab extra napkins.

places.name: Un Bien
places.notes: The Paseo family's own sandwich shack in Ballard. Pair it with a walk at the Locks.

places.name: Dick's Drive-In
places.notes: Cheap burgers, hand-cut fries and shakes since 1954. A Seattle rite of passage.

places.name: Molly Moon's Homemade Ice Cream
places.notes: Local ice cream with a line even in the rain. Salted caramel is the bestseller.

places.name: Caffe Vita
places.notes: The Capitol Hill roastery behind a lot of Seattle's coffee. Strong espresso, no fuss.

places.name: Zig Zag Café
places.notes: A cocktail bar tucked down the market stairs. It revived the Last Word, so order one.

places.name: Fremont Brewing
places.notes: A family-friendly beer garden near the canal. Try the Interurban IPA.

places.name: Pike Place Market
places.notes: Fish throwers, flower stalls and the gum wall. Come early on a weekday before the crowds.

places.name: Space Needle
places.notes: The 1962 World's Fair tower, with a rotating glass floor. Go on a clear day for Mount Rainier.

places.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
places.notes: Dale Chihuly's glass art in galleries, a glasshouse and a garden. Stunning at dusk.

places.name: Museum of Pop Culture
places.notes: Jimi Hendrix, Nirvana and sci-fi, in Frank Gehry's crumpled metal building.

places.name: Seattle Art Museum
places.notes: Strong Northwest Coast Native art, and the giant Hammering Man out front.

places.name: Seattle Central Library
places.notes: Rem Koolhaas's glass-and-steel library. Ride to the tenth floor and spiral down.

places.name: Seattle Aquarium
places.notes: Sea otters, octopus and the creatures of Puget Sound, on Pier 59.

places.name: Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
places.notes: A free museum on how Seattle outfitted the 1897 gold rush. Good with a Pioneer Square walk.

places.name: Wing Luke Museum
places.notes: Asian Pacific American history in an old hotel. Take the tour of the restored rooms.

places.name: Seattle Ferry Terminal
places.notes: Ride the ferry to Bainbridge Island for the cheapest skyline cruise in town.

places.name: Museum of History & Industry
places.notes: Seattle's story from logging to Boeing to grunge, in an old naval armory on Lake Union.

places.name: Hiram M. Chittenden Locks
places.notes: Watch boats rise and fall, and salmon climb the fish ladder from July to September.

places.name: Fremont Troll
places.notes: A giant troll crushing a real Volkswagen under the Aurora Bridge. Climb on for a photo.

places.name: Burke Museum
places.notes: Natural history and Native culture, with working labs you can watch through the glass.

places.name: The Museum of Flight
places.address: 9404 E Marginal Way S, Seattle, WA 98108
places.notes: Walk through a Concorde and Air Force One. Worth half a day.

places.name: Discovery Park
places.notes: The city's biggest park. Walk the loop trail down to the beach and the West Point lighthouse.

places.name: Kerry Park
places.notes: The postcard view of the Space Needle and Mount Rainier. Best at sunset.

places.name: Gas Works Park
places.notes: An old gas plant turned park on Lake Union. Fly a kite and watch the seaplanes land.

places.name: Olympic Sculpture Park
places.notes: Free outdoor sculpture zigzagging down to the water, with the Olympics across the Sound.

places.name: Volunteer Park
places.notes: A Victorian conservatory, a water tower to climb and the Asian Art Museum.

places.name: Washington Park Arboretum
places.notes: Miles of trails through trees from around the world, and a lovely Japanese garden.

places.name: Alki Beach Park
places.notes: A long sandy beach with skyline views. Take the water taxi over from downtown.
